findings.finding: Security note claim the plan does not support: 'there is no in-guest firewall to rely on, so administrator rights inside the guest do not open a path.' The plan says isolation is host-enforced and not built on in-guest firewall rules (lines 57-58, 155-156, 373-374). It never says that guest administrator rights cannot open a path, and it has not validated that. Isolation validation (chunk 4, line 449) and the graduation gate's adversarial agent (line 472) are not in Phase 1's 'Done & validated' list. The guest runs with an ephemeral autologon admin (line 343). The relay's isolation as written is IPv4 iptables (REDIRECT :80/:443/:53, FORWARD DROP); the plan says nothing on IPv6. The note's own TEST-08 bullet lists IPv6, SMB/NetBIOS and ICMP as vectors still to test. The note's header says it 'adds no design', and Decision 2 says the notes record only what each document's text says. This clause is an unvalidated assurance on the env-relay boundary.
findings.suggestion: In the design's Design section (line 441), then re-applied by implement, replace the clause with: 'there is no in-guest firewall, so the isolation argument does not rely on any in-guest control; whether a guest administrator can open a path is what the adversarial gate below must show, and the plan has not yet run it.'

findings.finding: 'The prepared Windows image (autounattend, first-boot task) is trusted input fixed before the build.' 'Fixed before the build' is supported: the image is prepared once and every build gets a per-build clone (lines 84-87, 336). 'Trusted' is not the plan's word. The plan calls the guest 'untrusted by design' (line 349), and the image carries an ephemeral autologon admin and a LabConfig bypass (lines 342-343). A reader could take 'trusted' as a security property rather than 'relied on'. This is graded SHOULD rather than MUST because, read as 'relied on' (part of the trusted computing base), it is accurate.
findings.suggestion: '...is input fixed at prepare, before the build (BOOT-06: it carries the startup hook, not build content)'. Or say 'relied on' instead of 'trusted'.

findings.finding: The note leaves out two boundary changes that the proposal's own text implies. (1) Action lifecycle step 4 (line 108): 'Inputs are staged from content-addressed storage into the sandbox.' The input root reaches the build environment outside the relay. BOOT-02 forbids that for context files, and only the cache key, not the ledger, records it. This is the proposal's largest env-relay change, and the note's 'Boundary' bullet does not name it. (2) The RE API gRPC service, CAS and ActionCache (lines 196-201) are a new network-facing service whose stored values feed parent ledgers. The note covers cache-entry forgery, but not the service as an attack surface. The note's claims are all supported, so this is an omission, not an unsupported claim.
findings.suggestion: Add to 'Boundary': 'action inputs are staged from CAS into the sandbox, outside the relay (Action execution lifecycle, step 4), which BOOT-02 does not allow today; the first design must route them through the relay or record them'. Add to 'What TEST-08 should exercise': 'an input root whose CAS blobs differ from their digests; an unauthenticated Execute or ActionCache write'.

informational.note: 'every Schannel and OpenSSL client ... trusts the relay's MITM CA' is slightly broader than the plan. Schannel trusts it through the machine root store; OpenSSL-based tools (conda, pip) trust it only through the SSL_CERT_FILE / REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE / CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO / NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS variables (lines 186-192). It is supported in substance, and it overstates exposure, not protection.

'per build, only the executor and its seed cross outside the relay (BOOT-02)' is supported by the built path: build.ps1 comes through the relay's cwd host (lines 46-48), and the CA through /ca.pem. bootstrap.md:49 lists the Windows seed as warden-io.exe and warden-run.ps1, and static addressing in the launcher is allowed (bootstrap.md:108-110). The plan's reuse list (lines 369-370) still names an older option with the build recipe on the seed disk. That option was not built, and the archive keeps it as written.

The open point 'recompute hermetic from the verified sub-ledger, never from the stored flag' partly restates the proposal (line 137: hermetic 'is recomputed from the ledger whenever the cache entry is validated'). The new part is 'verified'. Accurate.
